findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the package_index_probe rationale: the test runs `python -m build --outdir <dir> <tree>` (sdist then wheel, no PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR). Either match that or say the probe is a stricter, sdist-only variant of the same isolated-build hatchling fetch, and explain why PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR cannot cause a false refusal.
evidence: Plan: "This is the exact command and isolation path `tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py` uses."
tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py:28: `[sys.executable, "-m", "build", "--outdir", str(outdir), str(tree)]` (no --sdist)
`PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR` appears nowhere under tests/ (search returned no matches)
tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py:483 also uses `-m build --outdir` without --sdist
findings.finding: The plan says `sys.executable -m build --sdist --outdir <tmp>` with `PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1` 'is the exact command and isolation path `tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py` uses'. The code doesn't match: the test runs `[sys.executable, "-m", "build", "--outdir", str(outdir), str(tree)]`. That has no `--sdist`, so it builds an sdist and then a wheel from it. It also builds its env with `subprocess_env()` and never sets `PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR`.
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer trusts the 'exact command' claim and doesn't check whether the probe can pass while the tests still fail, or the other way round.
`PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1` makes the probe stricter than the tests it stands in for. On a host where a warm cache lets the tests pass, the preflight could still refuse.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'This is the exact command and isolation path ... uses' with: 'This uses the same isolated-build path (pip fetches `hatchling` into a fresh build env) as `tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py`, which runs `python -m build --outdir <dir> <tree>`. `--sdist` alone is enough because the sdist step already needs the network fetch. `PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1` is added on purpose so a warm cache cannot hide a denied index.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Change probe 3's 'as the detector backend does' to name the real source of the SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE/SEMGREP_LOG_FILE redirect: the test-session `configure_semgrep_settings_file` in tests/conftest.py and tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py. The backend's `--validate` call sets no env.
evidence: Plan: "`SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE` and `SEMGREP_LOG_FILE` pointed into the temp dir, as the detector backend does."
search 'SEMGREP_' in src/ → (no matches)
src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py:46-49: `harness.run_tool([binary, "--validate", "--config", det.source_path, "--metrics=off"], backend=BACKEND_OPENGREP)` with no env override
tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py:144-154 sets both vars under `repo_root / ".rebar" / "scratch" / f"pytest-sandbox-{os.getpid()}"`
findings.finding: The plan says semgrep_validate_probe points `SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE` and `SEMGREP_LOG_FILE` into the temp dir 'as the detector backend does'. The detector backend never sets them. `SEMGREP_` appears nowhere under src/, and `_opengrep_validate` just calls `harness.run_tool([...])`. The only code that sets them is the test-side `configure_semgrep_settings_file` (tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py:131-155, called from tests/conftest.py:214). It points them at `.rebar/scratch/pytest-sandbox-<pid>/semgrep.yml`, not a temp dir, and only after a settings-file probe succeeds.
scenarios: A maintainer reads 'as the detector backend does' and thinks production --validate runs already redirect semgrep's settings. Only the pytest session does that, so the probe actually copies the test harness setup, not the backend.
If configure_semgrep_settings_file's settings-file probe fails on some host, the test session runs semgrep with no redirect, but the preflight's redirected run could still pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'runs `<engine> --validate --config <one-rule temp file> --metrics=off` (the argv `_opengrep_validate` in src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py uses) with `SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE`/`SEMGREP_LOG_FILE` pointed into the temp dir, mirroring the redirect pytest sessions get from `configure_semgrep_settings_file` (tests/conftest.py).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make probe 2's command match `tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py:28` (drop `--sdist`), or reword the claim to 'the same isolated-build path, sdist only' and explain why the sdist is enough.

The test actually runs `[sys.executable, "-m", "build", "--outdir", str(outdir), str(tree)]` (line 28), which builds both an sdist and a wheel with no `--sdist` flag. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge in the plan and in docs/local-dev-env.md that any host lacking these capabilities (not only the agent sandbox) is refused. Document the partial-signal fallback `make lint typecheck import-convention test`, labelled as not equivalent to CI, and state that reverting the `verify: verify-host` prerequisite is the back-out.
evidence: '`verify` becomes `verify: verify-host`'
'No config key, environment variable, or command-line flag is added.'
The Docs bullet covers only 'the agent-sandbox case'
findings.finding: Making `verify` depend on `verify-host`, with no override, changes behavior for every host without outbound HTTPS to pypi.org/semgrep.dev, not only the agent sandbox. Examples are offline laptops, egress-restricted corporate networks and pip-mirror-only setups. Before this change, `make verify` there still ran lint, typecheck and the rest of the suite. The plan neither acknowledges this wider impact nor documents the fallback (invoking the gate targets directly) or a back-out path.
findings.location: Approach — Makefile bullet and 'No config key, environment variable, or command-line flag is added.'; Docs bullet
scenarios: A developer on a plane, or behind a proxy that blocks semgrep.dev, gets an outright refusal from `make verify` and does not know the individual gates can still be run.
A pip mirror configured via PIP_INDEX_URL serves hatchling, but semgrep.dev is blocked by policy; verify is permanently unusable on that host.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the 'Where `make verify` can run' subsection: 'On a host without these capabilities, `make lint typecheck import-convention test` still runs the gates but its verdict can differ from CI.' Add a rollback line to the plan: 'Back-out: drop `verify-host` from `verify`'s prerequisites.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how package_index_probe handles an absent `build` module: either fail with a distinct 'python -m build not installed' detail, or pass if test_build_provenance skips without it. Add a unit test for that case.

Contrast with probe 3: 'when neither `opengrep` nor `semgrep` is on PATH it passes (those tests skip without an engine)'
findings.finding: package_index_probe treats any failure of `sys.executable -m build` as a missing package-index capability. If the `build` module is not installed in the venv, the probe fails with 'No module named build' and the host is reported as lacking network access. The plan gives the semgrep probe a vacuous pass when its tool is absent ('those tests skip without an engine') but says nothing about the analogous case for `build`.
scenarios: A dev venv without `build` blocks `make verify` with a misleading package-index failure, even though test_build_provenance may skip or fail for a different reason.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define package_index_probe behaviour when `build` is not importable (pass/skip mirroring what test_build_provenance does, or a distinct 'build module missing' message), and add a test for it.
evidence: "run `sys.executable -m build --sdist --outdir <tmp>` on it"
"when neither `opengrep` nor `semgrep` is on PATH it passes (those tests skip without an engine)" — no analogous rule for `build`
"Each failed probe prints one line naming the capability and the error detail"
findings.finding: package_index_probe runs `sys.executable -m build`, but the plan does not handle the case where the `build` module (or a working hatchling build) is absent. The semgrep probe gets an explicit 'no engine → pass' arm; this probe has no equivalent. A missing `build` package fails with 'No module named build' and is reported as the outbound-HTTPS/package-index capability failing, misattributing a dependency gap to the network.
scenarios: A dev venv without the `build` package gets 'package index unreachable'-style refusal and is told to leave the sandbox, which does not help.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `importlib.util.find_spec('build')` first. If it is absent, follow the test suite's behaviour: pass if those tests skip, otherwise report 'python -m build not installed' as a distinct failure rather than a network one.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the disposition per probe failure arm: permanent (permission/denial, e.g. EPERM or sandbox deny → 'run outside the sandbox') versus transient (timeout, DNS/connection/5xx → 'retry'); reflect it in the printed line and test both.
evidence: "`make verify` needs these to give the same verdict as CI; run it where they are available (for an agent sandbox, outside it)"
"The probes are not retried: a transient network failure costs a re-run of a 10-second preflight"
"Exit 1 on any failure"
findings.finding: Every probe failure produces the same disposition: exit 1 plus a closing line telling the user to run it 'where they are available (for an agent sandbox, outside it)'. The plan itself calls some failures transient ('a transient network failure costs a re-run'), yet the surfaced remedy is the permanent one. A pypi.org/semgrep.dev outage, DNS blip or TimeoutExpired gets the same message as a sandbox `Operation not permitted` / `deny network-outbound` denial.
findings.location: Approach — closing line and 'The probes are not retried' paragraph
scenarios: A developer on a normal host during a PyPI incident is told to move out of a sandbox they are not in, instead of to retry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that every probe uses `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` (or try/finally removal) so its temp dir is removed on the pass, fail, timeout and exception paths.

"`SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE` and `SEMGREP_LOG_FILE` pointed into the temp dir"
Contrast probe 1: "in a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp()` directory, then remove it"
findings.finding: Only unix_socket_probe states that it removes its temp dir. package_index_probe and semgrep_validate_probe write a throwaway project, sdist output, settings file and log file into temp dirs, but the plan does not say these are cleaned up, including on the TimeoutExpired and exception paths. Every `make verify` run would leave temp dirs behind.
scenarios: Repeated verify runs accumulate tmp directories, including after timeouts.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each probe body in `with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:` so cleanup happens on all exit paths.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Weigh the known offline alternative to `--validate` (scan an empty directory for parse/schema validation; upstream semgrep#4620/#10375, opengrep#65) against requiring semgrep.dev, and record the decision with its reason in Verified cause / Approach.
evidence: Plan: "These are not test defects: CI hosts provide both capabilities, and a per-test shim cannot cover them because the denied capability is the operation under test."

Plan: "validation retries for about 60 s and the harness abstains. This fails 4 tests in ... test_code_review_conflict_markers.py / test_code_review_public_exposure.py ... and 2 in tests/unit/grounding/test_conformance.py"
src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py:46-48 runs `[binary, "--validate", "--config", det.source_path, "--metrics=off"]` for every detector source in production.
Upstream (semgrep#10375): the hard-coded `p/semgrep-rule-lints` stops `semgrep --validate` from running without access to semgrep.dev.

Prior art (koblas/exemplar PR #140): validation was changed to scan an empty directory with the rule, which checks parsing and schema only, so it works offline. The trade-off is that the rule lints no longer run.
findings.finding: The plan treats semgrep.dev access as a fixed host requirement and does not consider the known upstream limitation or the published offline workaround. `--validate`'s network fetch of `p/semgrep-rule-lints` has been reported upstream several times without a fix (semgrep#4454, #10375, #4620; opengrep#65). Other projects work around it by checking rule parsing and schema with a scan of an empty directory instead of `--validate`, which needs no network. Here the network call comes from product code (`_opengrep_validate` in src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py:46-48), not from the tests. So the plan's reason for not fixing it ("a per-test shim cannot cover them because the denied capability is the operation under test") does not hold for the 6 semgrep failures. The tests check conflict-marker and public-exposure detection, not network-based linting.
scenarios: A rebar user or agent runs code review on an air-gapped or sandboxed host. Each detector source waits about 60 s on retries and then abstains, so findings are silently lost. The preflight only protects `make verify`, not this product path.
semgrep.dev is down or changes the `p/semgrep-rule-lints` pack. `make verify` and CI then fail, or detectors become invalid, for reasons unrelated to the change being verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Alternatives considered' note. Either (a) open a follow-up ticket to replace `_opengrep_validate`'s network-dependent `--validate` with offline parse/schema validation (for example, scanning an empty directory and treating exit 7/2/8 as invalid), which would make the semgrep probe unnecessary; or (b) state why rule-lint validation against semgrep.dev must stay in the product path, for example because the lints catch real detector bugs, and keep the probe.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that `semgrep_validate_probe` resolves the engine as `which('opengrep') or which('semgrep')`, the same order as the backend's `_OPENGREP_CANDIDATES`, and test that opengrep is chosen when both are present.
evidence: Plan: "when neither `opengrep` nor `semgrep` is on PATH it passes ... otherwise it runs `<engine> --validate ...`"
src/rebar/grounding/engine_b.py:34: `_OPENGREP_CANDIDATES = ("opengrep", "semgrep")` — "we prefer an ``opengrep`` binary and fall back to ``semgrep``"
tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py:141: `binary = shutil.which("opengrep") or shutil.which("semgrep")`
findings.finding: The semgrep probe does not say which engine to pick when both `opengrep` and `semgrep` are on PATH. The detector backend always prefers opengrep (`_OPENGREP_CANDIDATES = ("opengrep", "semgrep")`). If the probe validated with the other binary, it could pass or refuse based on an engine the tests never run. For example, if opengrep's `--validate` does not fetch `p/semgrep-rule-lints`, probing semgrep instead would wrongly refuse a host.
scenarios: A host with both binaries installed where only one of them reaches semgrep.dev during `--validate`.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify engine = which('opengrep') or which('semgrep') (the backend's order), and add a unit test whose injected `which` returns both and asserts that opengrep's path is in the runner argv.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Have semgrep_validate_probe pick the engine as `which("opengrep") or which("semgrep")`, matching engine_b._OPENGREP_CANDIDATES, and say which engine the semgrep.dev fetch was observed on.
evidence: Plan: 'when neither `opengrep` nor `semgrep` is on PATH it passes ... otherwise it runs `<engine> --validate ...`'
src/rebar/grounding/engine_b.py:34 `_OPENGREP_CANDIDATES = ("opengrep", "semgrep")` and _resolve_binary returns the first found
tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py:141 uses `shutil.which("opengrep") or shutil.which("semgrep")`
Evidence class: Partially-verified (the network fetch was seen for one engine; which one, and whether the other does the same, is unstated)
findings.finding: The plan does not say which engine the semgrep probe runs when both `opengrep` and `semgrep` are on PATH. The backend whose failures the probe stands in for resolves engines in the order ('opengrep', 'semgrep') (engine_b._OPENGREP_CANDIDATES via _resolve_binary). opengrep is a fork, and the semgrep.dev ruleset download was observed for 'the opengrep/semgrep backend' without saying which binary did it. If the probe picks the other binary, it can pass where the tests fail, or fail where they pass.
scenarios: A host has both binaries and the probe runs `semgrep`, while the tests use `opengrep`, whose `--validate` behaves differently with the network denied.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose the binary with `which("opengrep") or which("semgrep")`, the same order as engine_b._resolve_binary. Add a unit test showing opengrep is chosen when both are present.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either run the three probes concurrently with an overall timeout well under 300 s, or replace the '10-second preflight' claim with the real pass- and fail-path costs (including semgrep's ~60 s retry inside the sandbox).
evidence: Plan: "so validation retries for about 60 s and the harness abstains"
Plan: probes 2 and 3 each use "`timeout=300`"; nothing says the probes run concurrently
Plan: "a transient network failure costs a re-run of a 10-second preflight, not of a 25-minute suite"
findings.finding: The plan justifies 'no retries' by calling the preflight a '10-second preflight', but the design does not deliver that on the failure path the plan is built for. The probes run one after another, each with `timeout=300`. In the sandbox, the plan itself says semgrep validation 'retries for about 60 s', and pip's own connection retries add more. Refusing the agent sandbox therefore takes over a minute, and the worst case if probes hang is about 10 minutes. On the passing path, a clean no-cache hatchling download plus a semgrep start-up also runs well past 10 s.
findings.location: Approach → probe timeouts / "The probes are not retried: a transient network failure costs a re-run of a 10-second preflight"
scenarios: An agent in the sandbox runs `make verify` and waits over 60 s (or up to ~10 min if a request hangs) for the refusal the plan presents as near-instant.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the probes in a ThreadPoolExecutor (each still injectable), so the wall time is that of the slowest probe, and use per-probe timeouts sized to the observed ~60 s semgrep retry (e.g. 120 s). State the measured pass-path cost in the docs instead of '10 seconds'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the '10-second preflight' claim: state whether the three probes run concurrently, size the timeouts from the observed ~60 s semgrep retry, and record the measured preflight wall time (sandboxed and unsandboxed) in the manual AC evidence.
evidence: 'so validation retries for about 60 s and the harness abstains'
'with `timeout=300`' (stated for both package_index_probe and semgrep_validate_probe)
'a re-run of a 10-second preflight, not of a 25-minute suite'
No statement of serial vs concurrent probe execution; no timing measurement in Testing or the ACs
findings.finding: The plan calls the preflight a '10-second preflight', but its own facts contradict that. The Verified-cause section says semgrep `--validate` retries for about 60 s when semgrep.dev is denied. Each network probe also has a 300 s timeout, and the plan does not say whether the probes run serially or concurrently. Inside the sandbox (the main target) the preflight could take one to several minutes, and up to about 10 minutes if both probes hang. No measurement of the preflight's wall time is planned.

findings.finding: The AF_UNIX probe can refuse hosts whose tests would actually pass, for two reasons. (1) On a platform with no AF_UNIX, the tests skip, but the probe would hit an AttributeError, which the plan reports as 'capability failing'. (2) The probe binds an absolute path inside `tempfile.mkdtemp()`, which can exceed the ~104-byte sun_path limit when TMPDIR is long, giving an OSError that is unrelated to the sandbox. `test_network_guard_local_ipc.py` avoids this by chdir-ing and binding a short relative name. The plan already handles the 'no engine on PATH' case for semgrep, but has no matching rule here.
scenarios: A contributor whose TMPDIR is long (e.g. a nested macOS /var/folders path or a custom TMPDIR) gets `make verify` refused with 'AF_UNIX sockets' even though every AF_UNIX test passes on their host.
A host whose Python has no socket.AF_UNIX is refused, although both AF_UNIX test modules skip there.
findings.suggested_fix: In unix_socket_probe: if not hasattr(socket, 'AF_UNIX'), return (True, 'AF_UNIX not provided by this platform; dependent tests skip'). Otherwise bind a short socket name relative to the mkdtemp directory (e.g. temporarily chdir into it, as test_network_guard_local_ipc does) so path length is never the failure.
